chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid; and ʿAli ibn al-Nuʿman, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who performed tamattuʿ and did not find a sacrificial offering. He said: He should fast three days in Makkah and seven when he returns to his family. If his companions do not wait for him and he is unable to remain in Makkah, then let him fast ten days when he returns to his family.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These two reports do not contradict the report of Rifaʿah that we cited in the first chapter, in his statement, ‘He fasts while he is traveling,’ because he did not make fasting during travel obligatory and nothing beyond that. Rather, he intended to clarify the permissibility of fasting these days during travel, in response to those who disallowed it and did not permit fasting them during travel. That which further clarifies what we have mentioned is that he intended choice in that matter.

key_terms.التَّخْيِيرَ: the allowance of choice between legally valid options
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the three days of fasting associated with the pilgrimage ruling
key_terms.مُسَافِرٌ: a traveler, in the context of fasting during travel
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering required in the pilgrimage context
key_terms.يَصُومُ: he fasts as a substitute act of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for fasting the substitute days of hajj tamattuʿ if the pilgrim cannot offer a sacrifice or remain in Makkah?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for one performing hajj al-tamattuʿ who cannot find the sacrificial offering, stating that he fasts three days in Makkah and seven after returning home. It also explains that if remaining in Makkah is not possible, fasting all ten days after returning is allowed, and the compiler clarifies that fasting these days during travel is permissible rather than obligatory.
